import importlib.util
for name in ('pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL'):
    print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
out = Path('tmp/pdfs')
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
print('Pages:', len(reader.pages))
print('Metadata:', reader.metadata)
for i, p in enumerate(reader.pages):
    t = p.extract_text()
    (out / f'page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(t)
(out / 'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages)))
print((out / 'page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-09.txt tmp/pdfs/page-10.txt tmp/pdfs/page-11.txt tmp/pdfs/page-12.txt tmp/pdfs/page-13.txt tmp/pdfs/page-14.txt'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
folder = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for page in range(1, 15):
    for extension in ('txt', 'png'):
        (folder / f'page-{page:02d}.{extension}').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(folder / 'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
folder.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary PDF inspection files.')
PY"

strengths: The method addresses an important computer vision problem: distilling large image datasets into compact training sets. Combining representative feature targets with per-class BatchNorm regularization provides an understandable, practical extension of SRe2L.

Table I demonstrates consistent improvements over the strengthened SRe2L baseline. On ImageNet-1K, accuracy increases from 54.4% to 57.6% at 50 images per class and from 58.3% to 60.7% at 100 images per class. Evaluation spans three datasets and four compression budgets, with three-run statistics for most main results.

Reporting both published and reproduced SRe2L results is valuable, especially because the reproduction substantially improves the baseline. The manuscript credits its main dependencies, including SRe2L, the barycenter algorithm, and POT, and supplies recovery hyperparameters.

The ablations, regularization sensitivity analysis, and transfer experiments provide useful additional evidence. In particular, ImageNet synthetic data transfer successfully to larger ResNets, reaching 62.2% with ResNet-101 at 50 images per class.
weaknesses: The central novelty is insufficiently established. Equation (4) approximates one empirical distribution per class using a limited number of support points. For the unregularized squared-Euclidean, p=2 formulation with freely optimized masses, this is equivalent to k-means quantization. The manuscript neither explains this relationship nor compares against k-means feature targets using the same image-recovery pipeline. The multi-distribution barycenter illustration does not resolve this concern.

Table III attributes most of the improvement at 10 images per class to per-class BatchNorm. Holding cross-entropy and per-class BatchNorm fixed, adding the barycenter term changes accuracy by -0.1, +0.8, and +0.5 percentage points on ImageNette, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K, respectively. These results support a useful regularization modification but provide limited evidence for the claimed advantage of Wasserstein matching. Controlled comparisons with alternative feature targets and MMD, including at larger budgets, are needed.

The connection between the optimized distribution and student training is incomplete. Equation (3) and Algorithm 3 learn nonuniform support masses, but Algorithm 1 outputs only images, Equation (5) matches targets uniformly, and the training description does not explain whether the learned masses affect sampling or loss weighting. Consequently, the student’s training distribution is not shown to correspond to the optimized Wasserstein approximation.

The transport computation is underspecified. Section III-B describes entropy regularization, whereas Appendix A presents an unregularized linear program and exact transport updates. The implemented regularized objective, entropy coefficient, initialization, and stopping criteria are missing. These are consequential reproducibility details for the central component.

The efficiency claim lacks comparative evidence. Table IV reports a single image-update timing on 64×64 ImageNette without baseline timings. The supplementary 14-hour ImageNet run does not provide a stage breakdown or matched comparison that establishes the additional cost of feature extraction and barycenter computation.

Evidence for improved diversity and generalization is less conclusive than the discussion suggests. Table II contains no competing-method transfer results, while the t-SNE embeddings are learned using real/synthetic mixtures. These experiments do not isolate whether Wasserstein matching improves distribution coverage or reduces reliance on background shortcuts.
